newsitem.title: USA: Merrill Lynch names Komansky CEO, chairman.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch names Komansky CEO, chairman.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co said on Monday that David Komansky, currently president and chief operating officer, will assume the additional title and responsibilities of chief executive officer on December 28, and of chairman of the board on April 15, 1997.
Merrill said its board of directors elected Komansky to the positions at its regular meeting today.
Chairman and CEO Daniel Tully, who turns 65 in 1997 and has served as CEO since May 1992, said he will continue as chairman of the board until his planned retirement on April 15, 1997.

"We have entered a period of enormous change for the financial services industry, and Merrill Lynch's financial strength, strategic agility, global market presence and trusted brand name will be unique assets," Komansky said.
"I am eager to work with all my colleagues at Merrill Lynch to take full advantage of the changing environment for our clients, shareholders and employees," he added in a statement.

Komansky was named president and COO on January 25, 1995, and serves as one of three employee directors on Merrill's 14-member board, and as a member of the office of chairman and office of chief executive.

Prior to that, he served from 1993 to 1995 as executive vice president, global debt and equity markets group, with executive management responsibility for debt and equity trading and institutional sales on a global basis.
